target_profile.system_boundary: Captured go.etcd.io/raft/v3 library including raft state machine, Node/RawNode adapters, membership/quorum, log and MemoryStorage; external caller provides real persistence, network and application.
protocol_contexts: Node identity, current term/role, local applied simple or joint voter configuration, log entry term/index, read request context.
ownership: Node loop serializes raft; RawNode callers serialize externally.
Caller owns durability, message delivery, ordered application and client retries.

activities.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement
activities.realization_summary: Proposal, append acceptance and voter Match aggregation form committed prefixes.

activities.purpose: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority
activities.realization_summary: Term dispatch, campaigns, role reset, quorum checking and transfer qualify authority and stale work.

activities.purpose: Recovery and resynchronization of eligible participation
activities.realization_summary: Snapshot catch-up and startup restore rebuild eligible history and configuration.
Applied configuration entries update simple/joint voter and learner membership.
Ready/apply responses track committed work delivery and application progress. External state-machine execution belongs to caller.

activities.purpose: History, persistence and reconstruction of support
activities.realization_summary: Ready/storage response protocol manages unstable history; disk durability is caller-owned and MemoryStorage is provided.

activities.purpose: Client contracts, invocation intervals and observed completion
activities.realization_summary: Node/RawNode expose proposals, read-index and Ready consumption with retries and application duties.

behaviors.protocol_context: One raft node, current term and role
behaviors.trigger: Incoming higher/lower-term message, election outcome, check-quorum loss or leadership transfer
implementation_guards: Higher-term pre-vote requests and granted pre-vote responses do not immediately change the local term; in-lease vote requests are ignored unless transfer-forced.
Lower-term responses are ignored before role dispatch; old storage snapshot completion remains applicable.
writes: Term and Vote on term change; role, lead, timers, per-peer progress, election votes and readOnly tracking on reset.
important_branches: Pre-candidate transition resets votes and leader without incrementing term or resetting all progress.
Reset preserves the committed log and pendingReadIndexMessages; it replaces the separate readOnly acknowledgment tracker.
Transfer pauses proposals, catches the target up and sends TimeoutNow; election timeout aborts an unfinished transfer.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Clears old vote and peer progress aggregation; incoming message term qualifies its consumption.
cross_activity_effects.A5: Committed snapshot/application completions retain meaning across terms.

behaviors.trigger: Tick timeout, Campaign or TimeoutNow; vote response
implementation_guards: Campaign requires nonlearner local progress, no pending snapshot, and no unapplied committed configuration change.
Vote grant checks prior vote/leader and candidate last term/index; vote aggregation uses voter membership and first recorded vote per node.
external_effects: Campaign sends requests to union of active voters and defers self vote until persistence; a winning pre-vote starts real election, a winning election becomes leader and broadcasts its initial empty entry.

cross_activity_effects.A1: A winning joint or simple voter quorum grants the role which can form new log decisions.

behaviors.execution_owner: leader stepLeader, appendEntry, maybeCommit and tracker quorum
behaviors.protocol_context: Current leader term, active voter sets, per-peer Match
implementation_guards: Reject proposals when removed or transferring; validate pending and joint configuration proposals unless validation disabled.
Only tracked peers reach response handling; Match support is aggregated over voters, both joint halves, and commit requires a newer index whose log term equals the leader term.
writes: New entry indexes and terms; per-peer Match/Next and flow state; committed index.
external_effects: Successful append-response commitment releases pending pre-current-term reads then broadcasts appends. Other successful acknowledgment branches retry replication or finish catch-up for transfer.
Heartbeats advertise min(peer Match, committed), not an unmatched commit index.
async_boundaries: Local append self acknowledgment is deferred through storage/Advance.

cross_activity_effects.A7: The append-response commit branch explicitly releases postponed read requests.

implementation_guards: Append checks predecessor term, refuses overwriting committed entries, and caps propagated commit at the supplied matching suffix.
If predecessor is already below committed, reply with committed index without replacing committed history.
writes: Conflicting uncommitted suffix, committed index, leader and election elapsed.
external_effects: Append success/rejection goes through durability-dependent send; heartbeat echoes read context and commits the bounded index produced by leader.

cross_activity_effects.A2: Accepted leader traffic refreshes leader identity and election timeout.

behaviors.protocol_context: Applied log configuration, incoming/outgoing voters and staged learners
behaviors.trigger: Application applies committed configuration change or recovery installs ConfState
legal_preconditions: Application applies committed configuration changes in order and records returned ConfState in snapshots.
implementation_guards: Simple changes alter at most one voter and cannot run in joint state; reject zero incoming voters.
Joint entry retains outgoing voter set; demoted outgoing voters remain staged learners until joint exit.
writes: Configuration and progress maps; local learner status.
important_branches: Removed/demoted leader steps down only when stepDownOnRemoval is set, then returns.
For a remaining leader, maybeCommit can advance committed under new quorum; this branch broadcasts but does not call releasePendingReadIndexMessages. Otherwise it probes new peers.
Removed transfer target aborts transfer. Existing progress is copied; new peers start with Match zero.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Reinterprets eligible Match support under the new voter quorum.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Changes promotion/transfer eligibility and may remove leadership.

unknowns: Can configuration-driven first current-term commitment coexist legally with a postponed read, given campaign and application-order guards?

behaviors.execution_owner: RawNode Ready/acceptReady/Advance and unstable; caller storage worker
behaviors.protocol_context: Synchronous Ready or AsyncStorageWrites local append stream
behaviors.trigger: Outstanding entries, HardState, snapshot or delayed responses
legal_preconditions: Async append requests are reliably processed in order per target; writes are durable before releasing attached responses.
Synchronous Ready/Advance follows persistence and completion requirements; README same-batch messaging exception conflicts with Ready documentation and is retained as a surface.
writes: Accepted unstable work progress; persisted completion trims matching unstable entries; previous Ready state and delayed self steps.
durable_effects: Library emits work and consumes reported completion; actual durability belongs to caller. MemoryStorage itself is in-memory.
important_branches: Storage append responses include current term plus entry term/index; old-term completion cannot trim entries, though a carried committed snapshot still completes.
Term-changing HardState work also carries completion for outstanding entries, avoiding reliance on a new proposal to trim old unstable work.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Defers publication of append support and leader self support until caller persistence.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Defers election self vote and remote vote replies; generation qualifies completion.

behaviors.protocol_context: Storage startup or leader snapshot recovery
implementation_guards: Load HardState commit within stored log range; restore snapshot only if beyond committed and local node belongs to snapshot configuration.
Matching snapshot term/index only fast-forwards commit; nonmatching snapshot replaces unstable history and reconstructs configuration.
writes: Committed index, recovered Term/Vote, configuration and unstable snapshot; startup role becomes follower.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Restores committed prefix and eligible configuration rather than old volatile vote/replication tallies.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Pending snapshot prevents promotion until completion.

behaviors.execution_owner: raftLog delivery, raft.appliedTo/appliedSnap and caller apply worker
behaviors.protocol_context: Committed prefix and ordered application stream
behaviors.trigger: Ready delivery, MsgStorageApplyResp or snapshot append completion
implementation_guards: Do not deliver entries while a snapshot is pending; async mode caps delivery at locally stable prefix.
Applied index is bounded by committed; raft.appliedTo takes max with previous applied to tolerate older completion.
writes: Applying/applied indexes and outstanding byte accounting.
important_branches: If leader in AutoLeave configuration and applied index reaches pendingConfIndex, propose empty configuration change; transfer may drop it.
Synchronous Node interface permits Advance during application, so internal applied bookkeeping need not prove external state-machine completion. Async response contract explicitly follows completion.

cross_activity_effects.A4: Application progress can initiate automatic joint exit.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Applied configuration progress affects campaign admission.

unknowns: If auto-leave proposal is dropped during leadership transfer and transfer times out with no further application, what event retries automatic joint exit?

behaviors.protocol_context: ReadOnlySafe read context under current leader, or lease-based variant
behaviors.trigger: MsgReadIndex, current-term commit release or heartbeat acknowledgment
legal_preconditions: Caller correlates request context and waits for local application past returned index before serving the read; requests may be lost and caller retries.
implementation_guards: Non-singleton leader postpones until current-term committed entry; safe mode requires current voter quorum heartbeat acknowledgment.
Duplicate context is ignored while already tracked; contexts identify pending requests.
writes: pendingReadIndexMessages before current-term commit; separate readOnly map/queue and acknowledgment sets after release; readStates for local delivery.
important_branches: Singleton read returns current committed immediately; lease-based mode omits heartbeat quorum after gate.
Reset clears readOnly but retains pre-gate pending messages; release re-enters safe-mode tracking at then-current committed index.
Heartbeat acknowledgment of later queued read releases all earlier read contexts.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Consumes committed prefix and quorum-confirmed authority for read-index output.

behaviors.trigger: Proposal, receive, tick, configuration, Ready and Advance channel selection
implementation_guards: Node loop serializes state-machine actions; synchronous mode withholds next Ready until Advance.
Responses from untracked nonlocal peers are filtered. RawNode is thread-unsafe and caller serialization is required.
external_effects: Ready exports persistence/application/messages/read states. Proposal acceptance is not commit completion, and retries are caller-owned.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Routes serialized inputs into formation; filters unknown response sources.
cross_activity_effects.A4: Routes application configuration updates into changer.

facts.meaning: The local log records a committed prefix through index c. This alone is neither local durability nor completed external application, and does not imply that every establishment path schedules the same follow-up.
facts.validity_context: Local retained history; leader aggregation additionally tests candidate index term against current Term. Membership can change what support qualifies. Reset preserves committed history.
facts.durability: Published as HardState; recovered from caller storage or snapshot. In-memory commitment may precede local persistence.
facts.recovery: newRaft/loadState and snapshot restore recover bounded committed prefix.

facts.meaning: The local tracker contains active incoming voters, optional outgoing voters, learners and staged learners with corresponding progress; eligibility is local applied/recovered configuration, not universal knowledge of the latest change.
facts.validity_context: Until application or snapshot/restart installs another configuration; joint decisions require both voter majorities.
facts.durability: Returned ConfState must be included by caller in snapshots; configuration entries are persisted through normal log processing.
facts.recovery: confchange.Restore reconstructs sets and new progress from snapshot/Storage.InitialState.

facts.meaning: A non-singleton leader has retained a ReadIndex message pending a committed entry in its current term. The queue records an outstanding request, not a completed read or a quorum acknowledgment.
facts.validity_context: pendingReadIndexMessages survives reset; release checks current-term commitment and then processes requests using current read mode and commit index.
facts.durability: Volatile; requests may be lost according to Node contract.
facts.recovery: No restart reconstruction; caller retry is required.

surfaces.reason: Conflicting same-Ready persistence/send ordering statements. Example saves entries before sending, but does not resolve the weaker README permission.
Commit advancement here does not schedule postponed-read release; legal coexistence and applicable completion duty remain open.
AutoLeave proposal may be dropped during transfer; timeout aborts transfer without an explicit auto-leave retry. Need producer history and bounded completion contract.
Proposal channel is disabled on local removal but recalculated on leader changes; eligibility and intended forwarding after removal need further contract work.

surfaces.entry_point: Caller disk, network and state machine
surfaces.reason: Library emits Ready/local storage work and requires caller persistence, transport, correlation and application; MemoryStorage and in-repository adapters remain in scope.

formation.explanation: A leader assigns its term and next index to admitted proposals and sends append requests. Followers match predecessor term/index, preserve committed entries, replace conflicting uncommitted suffixes and report append support after caller persistence. Leader dispatch admits term-qualified tracked responses, updates Match, aggregates only current voters (both majorities when joint), and advances commit only when the selected index has the current leader term. Append-response advancement releases postponed reads and broadcasts decisions; configuration-driven advancement separately broadcasts without that release call. Heartbeats carry a commit capped by peer Match. Followers propagate commit into Ready application delivery, whose external completion is caller-owned.

context.explanation: Election starts only for a promotable voter without unapplied committed configuration changes or pending snapshot. Vote grants require permitted prior-vote state and an up-to-date candidate log; current voter majorities aggregate votes, with self vote deferred to persistence. Pre-vote preserves term/vote and successful pre-vote starts the real campaign. Winning election resets progress, installs leader role and appends a current-term empty entry. Higher terms usually force follower role, with explicit pre-vote and lease exceptions. Reset clears old vote/progress/readOnly support and transfer state but retains committed log and pre-gate pending reads. Lower-term replies are rejected before role consumption; old storage append completion cannot trim entries but committed snapshot completion remains valid. Quorum loss can remove leadership, and transfer catches up a voter then asks it to campaign, abandoning unfinished transfer on timeout.

connection.explanation: Authority is acquired with votes qualified by log history and local applied membership. Within that authority, durable append replies become eligible Match support for commit. Membership application changes which support is counted; outgoing voters remain required until joint exit, and learners do not count. Old volatile tallies are reset on authority transition, while committed history and term-independent application survive. Storage completions have separate generation checks before unstable history is discarded. Recovery reconstructs term/vote, committed history and configuration from caller storage rather than old volatile tallies. Read-index consumes both a current-term commitment gate and renewed quorum authority (except singleton/lease variants), with request identity and final read execution left to the caller. Node serialization and Ready ordering connect these mechanisms without making emitted work equivalent to completed external work.

open_details: README same-batch persistence exception conflicts with Ready interface; legality of that overlap remains unresolved.
Reachability and responsibility of postponed reads when configuration switch commits without release remain open; ReadIndex explicitly allows loss/retry.
AutoLeave retry after aborted transfer and no further application remains unexplained.
Detailed rejection-hint optimization, configuration validation override and mixed-version read retry semantics are not fully investigated.
core_overview.rationale: Representative formation and authority paths, their persistence/configuration/recovery support, old-message handling and application boundary have been traced. Remaining local questions are retained without treating this map as exhaustive coverage or evidence of correctness.
